5. The feature-geometry graph

Here every feature is a node, laid out on a circle in an order chosen by hierarchical clustering of |cos similarity|, with an edge drawn between any two non-orthogonal features. Node color/size encodes each feature's dimensionality. Disconnected components are tegum factors — independent, orthogonal sub-arrangements (e.g. a 3-clique triangle here, an isolated pair there) that combine to form the overall higher-dimensional Thomson-problem solution.
